assays.assay_description: Mice placed in a clear Plexiglass arena (27.31 × 27.31 × 20.32 cm, Med Associates ENV-510, ~330 lux); ambulation tracked by infrared beams for 30 min (with/without WAY-100635 pretreatment) or 120 min in a separate cohort. Total locomotion measured as an index of sedation (5-HT1A activation).

application_type.evidence: mice were administered either 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (0.1, 0.3, 1 or 3 mg/kg, s.c.) or 5-MeO-MET (0.3, 1, 3 or 10 mg/kg, s.c.) and immediately gently placed in a clear Plexiglass arena

setup_habituation.evidence: 'Male 10-15 week old C57BL/6J mice were allowed to habituate for 30 min' — the apparatus is not specified; the parallel HTR section states habituation was to the testing room, so apparatus habituation is not clearly described.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to ambulate freely for 30 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food is described in the Plexiglass arena during the recording session.

water_restriction.evidence: No water is described in the Plexiglass arena during the recording session.

time_to_assay.evidence: mice were administered either 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT ... or 5-MeO-MET ... and immediately gently placed in a clear Plexiglass arena

sample_size.evidence: Evaluation of 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT in open field for two hours (n = 3-4/group); Effect of WAY-100635 ... on total locomotion (n = 7-8/group, 30 min)

outcomes.summary: Both 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT and 5-MeO-MET produced dose-dependent suppression of locomotion (sedation) in the open field, with the lowest effective dose of 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT at 0.03 mg/kg. WAY-100635 pretreatment was used to probe 5-HT1A dependence of locomotor suppression. Locomotion was also recorded in socially defeated mice to exclude confounding sedation at 24 h.
outcomes.statistics: Analysis was done using one-way ANOVA with multiple comparisons with Tukey's post hoc test, and exact p values have been denoted in the Figure (Extended Data Fig. 7a,c,d).
outcomes.evidence: We observed dose-dependent locomotor suppression in the open-field test for both 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT and 5-MeO-MET (Extended Data Fig. 7).

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in a new observation cage after s.c. drug (4-F,5-MeO-PyrT or 5-MeO-MET), with or without WAY-100635 pretreatment (1 or 2 mg/kg, 15 min prior). Overhead camera (GoPro HERO9, 120 Hz); blinded observers counted head twitches during the first 10 min.

application_type.evidence: Mice were randomly administered with vehicle or WAY-100635 (1 mg/kg or 2 mg/kg, s.c.). Fifteen minutes after the pretreatment injection, mice were administered either 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT ... or 5-MeO-MET ... (s.c.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were habituated to the testing room for 30 min (room, not apparatus) and then '...placed in a new observation cage'.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were ... placed in a new observation cage. An overhead camera (GoPro HERO9 at 120 Hz) recorded their movements.

food_restriction.evidence: No food is described in the observation cage during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water is described in the observation cage during recording.

sample_size.evidence: Determination of optimal inhibitory WAY-100635 dose ... on total locomotion (n = 7-8/group) and HTR (n = 6/group).

outcomes.summary: 5-MeO-MET produced strong dose-dependent head twitches, particularly when co-administered with the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY-100635 (indicating 5-HT1A-mediated suppression of HTR). The 5-HT1A-selective analogue 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT produced no notable HTR up to 3 mg/kg, with or without WAY-100635.
outcomes.statistics: Analysis was done using one-way ANOVA with multiple comparisons with Tukey's post hoc test, and exact p values have been denoted in the Figure (Extended Data Fig. 7d).
outcomes.evidence: In HTR tests, 5-MeO-MET showed strong dose-dependent activity following co-administration of the 5-HT1A-selective antagonist WAY-100635. ... By contrast, 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT did not produce notable HTR at doses up to 3 mg/kg in the presence or absence of WAY-100635.

assays.assay_name: Social Interaction Test (after chronic social defeat stress)
assays.assay_description: Two-phase test on day 11, 24 h after s.c. 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (1 mg/kg) ± WAY-100635: no-target session (2.5 min exploration of an open-field arena with empty wire mesh enclosure) and target session (2.5 min with an unfamiliar CD-1 mouse inside the wire mesh enclosure). EthoVision tracking of time in the interaction zone (interaction ratio), corner time and distance moved.

application_type.evidence: we injected 1 mg/kg -1 of drug or vehicle (s.c.) 1 h after the last SD session on day 10, followed by the SI test 24 h after drug administration on day 11.

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation of the experimental mouse to the SI arena is described.

setup_restrain.evidence: the experimental mouse is allowed to explore an open-field arena for 2.5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food is described in the SI arena during the test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water is described in the SI arena during the test.

time_to_assay.evidence: mice were injected with 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (1.0 mg/kg) or vehicle and evaluated in the SI test 24 h later.

sample_size.evidence: A total of 46 mice were administered vehicle treatment (17 control, 29 stress), 53 received 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (17 control, 36 stress), 15 received WAY-100635 (5 control, 10 stress), and 29 received 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT + WAY-100635 (10 control, 19 stress).

outcomes.summary: Chronic social defeat reduced the interaction ratio (social avoidance) in vehicle-treated mice; a single dose of 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (1 mg/kg s.c.) given 24 h earlier restored the interaction ratio and reduced corner time in stressed mice, and increased the proportion of resilient animals, without altering locomotion. Co-administration of WAY-100635 blocked these effects, indicating 5-HT1A mediation.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA: interaction P = 0.1778, row (treatment) factor P = 0.0741, column (control/stress) factor P = 0.0001; Fisher's LSD post hoc comparisons with exact P values in figures; two-sided Fisher's exact test for resilient/susceptible proportions.
outcomes.evidence: This phenotype was rescued by 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT treatment, as indicated by an increased IR in the stress-exposed mice. ... WAY-100635 co-administration blocked the ability of 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT to ameliorate SI deficits in this model.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Interaction ratio of time in the interaction zone, 'the ratio of time spent in the corners of the chamber during the SI phase', and 'distance moved as a measure of locomotor activity' (Extended Data Fig. 7e-g).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Totals from the 2.5-min sessions are reported; no within-session time-course analysis.

B4_ethological.evidence: Outcomes are zone-based times (interaction zone, corner zone) automatically tracked with EthoVision — spatial measures rather than directly scored social acts (sniffing, following).

B5_social.evidence: a new CD-1 male mouse is placed into a wire mesh cage, which is situated along one side of the arena. This area is the interaction zone.

B6_cognitive.evidence: The test measures innate social approach/avoidance, not learning or memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: behaviour during the SI test ... was automatically tracked using EthoVision analysis software (Noldus).

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only univariate comparisons and a resilient/susceptible split based on the SI ratio are reported.

E1_environment_type.evidence: the experimental mouse is allowed to explore an open-field arena ... with a wire mesh cage situated along one side

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter or refuge is available to the focal mouse in the arena.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding is described in the SI arena.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material is described in the SI arena.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects are described; the wire mesh cage is the social stimulus holder.

E6_spatial.evidence: The arena is an open field with a virtual interaction zone and corner zones; no physical dividers separate areas accessible to the focal mouse.

E7_social_context.evidence: a new CD-1 male mouse is placed into a wire mesh cage, which is situated along one side of the arena.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water is present in the SI arena.

D1_continuity.evidence: The SI test is a two-session test consisting of a target and no-target session ... locomotion data were measured during the no-target session (both sessions recorded and reported).

D2_session_duration.evidence: the experimental mouse is allowed to explore an open-field arena for 2.5 min ... the test mouse is placed back into the arena for another 2.5 min.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Twenty-four hours after the last defeat bout, mice were tested in the SI test (day 11) — a single test day.

D4_baseline.evidence: The no-target session occurs after drug administration; no pre-drug SI recording is reported.

D5_followup.evidence: we injected 1 mg/kg of drug or vehicle (s.c.) 1 h after the last SD session on day 10, followed by the SI test 24 h after drug administration on day 11.

D6_circadian.evidence: Total recording was 5 min, far less than 6 h.

assays.assay_description: Individually housed mice (habituated to two water bottles on day 10) were given overnight ad libitum access to one bottle of water and one of 1% sucrose, immediately following the SI test on day 11; preference = sucrose/(sucrose+water) × 100. Groups: control/stress × vehicle, 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (1 mg/kg s.c.), WAY-100635, and combination.

application_type.evidence: we injected 1 mg/kg -1 of drug or vehicle (s.c.) 1 h after the last SD session on day 10

setup_habituation.evidence: On day 10, chronic SD stressed mice were individually housed and habituated to two bottles containing just water.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice had ad libitum overnight access to both bottles.

food_restriction.evidence: Mice were housed with food and water available ad libitum, and the test took place in the individual home cage with ad libitum overnight access to both bottles.

water_restriction.evidence: Mice had ad libitum overnight access to both bottles.

time_to_assay.evidence: Twenty-four hours later, following the SI test, one bottle was replaced with a 1% sucrose solution.

sample_size.evidence: A total of 27 mice were administered vehicle (9 control, 18 stress), 27 received 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (9 control, 18 stress), 15 received WAY-100635 (5 control, 10 stress), and 15 received 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT + WAY-100635 (5 control, 10 stress).

outcomes.summary: Socially defeated vehicle-treated mice showed reduced sucrose preference (anhedonia). A single dose of 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT (1 mg/kg s.c.) given 24 h earlier significantly increased sucrose preference in stressed mice to levels indistinguishable from non-stressed controls; co-administration of WAY-100635 reversed this effect.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA: interaction P = 0.0773, row (treatment) factor P = 0.0159, column (control/stress) factor P = 0.0008; Fisher's LSD post hoc with exact P values in Fig. 5e.
outcomes.evidence: stressed mice treated with 4-F,5-MeO-PyrT had significantly increased sucrose preference relative to vehicle-treated animals and were essentially indistinguishable from non-stressed mice treated with vehicle or drug.

B1_num_measures.evidence: preference for sucrose over water was calculated as follows: (sucrose/(sucrose + water)) × 100 — a single derived preference measure.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only total overnight consumption/preference is reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Only a consumption-derived preference score is reported; no natural behaviours were scored.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were individually housed for the two-bottle choice test; no social construct is measured.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Sucrose preference reflects innate hedonic drive, not a learned association.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Intake measured from bottles; no behavioural classification software reported.

E1_environment_type.evidence: On day 10, chronic SD stressed mice were individually housed and habituated to two bottles ... Mice had ad libitum overnight access to both bottles.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter in the testing cage is described.

E3_bedding.evidence: Bedding in the testing cage is not explicitly reported.

E4_nesting.evidence: Nesting material in the testing cage is not reported.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects are reported in the testing cage.

E6_spatial.evidence: A single individual housing cage with two drinking bottles.

E7_social_context.evidence: chronic SD stressed mice were individually housed

E8_food_water.evidence: Mice had ad libitum overnight access to both bottles (water and 1% sucrose).

D1_continuity.evidence: Mice had ad libitum overnight access to both bottles — uninterrupted overnight (>6 h) measurement of intake.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Mice had ad libitum overnight access to both bottles, and preference for sucrose over water was calculated.

D3_recording_days.evidence: A single overnight two-bottle choice measurement following the SI test is reported.

D4_baseline.evidence: Habituation was to two bottles containing just water; no baseline preference data are reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Drug was given on day 10, 1 h after the last defeat; the sucrose test followed the SI test performed 24 h after drug administration on day 11.

D6_circadian.evidence: Mice had ad libitum overnight access to both bottles (>6 h).

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed on the same four behavioural assays (open field locomotion, HTR, social interaction test, sucrose preference test); cryo-EM structures, BRET/cAMP/arrestin/uptake assays, pharmacokinetics and plasma/brain binding were correctly excluded as non-behavioural.

Open-field locomotion: scored as ONE assay spanning the 30-min (± WAY-100635) and 120-min cohorts and both compounds, per the rubric's dose/timepoint collapsing rule; corner time and distance moved in Extended Data Fig. 7e,g were assigned to the SI assay because the Methods state locomotion was measured during the SI no-target session.
B1 for the open field set to 0 (total locomotion only); deepseek's '2-3' relied on corner time that belongs to the SI assay, and gemma's score/value were internally inconsistent.

SI test B4 scored 0 (overriding two candidates): outcomes are EthoVision zone-occupancy times (interaction zone, corner), which the rubric explicitly classifies as spatial rather than ethological measures.

SI test E6 scored 0 (overriding two candidates): the apparatus is an open-field arena with a virtual interaction zone and a stimulus-holding wire mesh cage, which the rubric treats as a single open space.

D5 (post-acute follow-up) set to Yes for both SI and sucrose preference assays, overriding all candidates: drug was injected on day 10 and testing occurred 24 h later on day 11, meeting the ≥24 h criterion.

Sucrose preference D1 scored 2 (continuous monitoring) for consistency with D2 (>6 h overnight) and D6 (yes); E3 bedding scored 0 because home-cage bedding is not explicitly stated (no inference permitted).

Housing handling set to 'yes' (overriding all candidates' 'not_reported') because the Methods explicitly state 'Control mice were housed in pairs ... and handled daily'; confidence medium because this applies to the social-defeat control cohort.

WAY-100635 (5-HT1A antagonist) was not given a dosing entry as it is a pharmacological control antagonist rather than a psychedelic/test compound; its doses (1 and 2 mg/kg s.c., 15 min pretreatment) are described in the assay descriptions.
